messages:
julia-support: Heads-up — ACME reported a strange sawtooth pattern in the tokens/sec and TTFT panels starting ~10:00 UTC. They say values jump up for one minute, drop to near-zero the next, and repeat. Screenshot attached in ticket.

mike-sre: Seen this before? Could be a rollup/aggregation boundary issue or consumer rebalances. Any quick checks I should run on prod streams?

sara-ps: I'm on the call with ACME. They say the app traffic is steady (no real throughput swings). They provided a short server log showing monotonic token emission.

leo-ml: Two quick hypotheses: 1) the streaming aggregator is double-counting on certain windows then correcting (sawtooth), 2) window alignment uses event_time vs ingestion_time mismatch causing oscillation. Also possible intermittent key-partition hot-swap where one aggregator empties partial state then another replays.

mike-sre: I'll tail the aggregator logs for the affected time window. Running this against the metrics backend now:

```
curl -s "https://metrics.redwood.internal/query" -d "q=SELECT sum(tokens) as t FROM streaming_rollup WHERE service='api' AND window=60s GROUP BY window ORDER BY window DESC LIMIT 10"
```

metrics-bot: query returned windows: [0, 1200, 0, 1195, 0, 1189, 0]

mike-sre: That looks like exact sawtooth. Not consistent with downstream ingestion — the upstream producer logs show ~1200 tokens/min steady.

sara-ps: Customer is escalating — billing spike visible because our per-token billing uses the same rollup. They're worried about overcharges during spikes.

leo-ml: Can you check if the rollup job emits partial checkpoints or deletes state between windows? If aggregator TTL < window retention, it might drop partial aggregates mid-run and then next micro-batch re-emits full counts.

mike-sre: Found this in aggregator logs around the windows:
```
WARN 2026-07-14T10:00:59Z AggregateEvictor - evicted key shard-17 due to memory pressure
INFO 2026-07-14T10:01:00Z WindowEmitter - emitting window start=10:01:00 tokens=1198
INFO 2026-07-14T10:02:00Z WindowEmitter - emitting window start=10:02:00 tokens=0
```

mike-sre: So eviction happens right before a window emit, then a reconciliation emits 0 (because partial state lost) then next batch re-aggregates and emits full count — explains sawtooth.

leo-ml: Why would eviction spike exactly at minute boundaries? Could be GC pauses on the JVM or periodic memory cleanup, or our batching micro-scheduler aligning evictions with the window tick.

julia-support: Customer wants repro steps. Anyone can provide a deterministic repro or mitigation we can apply quickly?

mike-sre: Quick mitigation: increase aggregator memory pool or bump eviction threshold; longer term: persist partial state to local disk snapshots before eviction or change eviction to prefer oldest keys with backoff.

sara-ps: We should also avoid billing on raw rollup feed until we have monotonic counters enforced. Can we switch billing to use deduplicated cumulative counters for pending invoices?

leo-ml: Yes — we can derive a monotonic counter from total_tokens (client-side monotonic) and compute deltas server-side in an idempotent reducer. Short-term toggle: route billing to cumulative_counter stream (already available) instead of minute rollup.

deploybot: scheduled job "metrics-billing-toggle" at 2026-07-14T10:35Z to flip billing source to cumulative_counter (dry-run mode first).

mike-sre: Repro steps I used locally to simulate: run two aggregator instances with small mem limit and start synthetic producer:
```
./bin/synthetic-producer --rate 20k/min --fixed-timestamp
AGG_MEM_LIMIT=64m ./bin/aggregator --partitions=8
```

That reproduces sawtooth within ~5 minutes.

leo-ml: Added a monitoring alert to catch evictions occurring within 5s of window boundaries: alert if eviction_count/window_emit_delta < 5s. Also instrumented emitter to emit debug metrics when eviction occurs.

julia-support: Next actions for support team: 1) notify ACME of mitigation (billing source flip) 2) schedule customer-facing postmortem 3) follow-up once patch merged. I'll draft message.

sara-ps: ACME confirmed temporary billing flip is fine. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

metrics-bot: patch branch created: fix/avoid-evict-on-window-boundary (#4821)

mike-sre: I'll open a runbook section for this and coordinate the memory threshold rollback once patch is live.

julia-support: Closing loop here after deploy. Will update ticket when deploy finishes.
